requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: A 1 GiB LUKS1 container was created with an active AES-XTS dm-crypt mapping, formatted as XFS, mounted read/write at /srv/secure, and shown to contain readable marker data. The key and backing file were root-owned with restrictive permissions.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume must unlock and mount automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: crypttab and fstab declarations generated the expected systemd units. Activation succeeded from a deliberately inactive state. A bounded reboot then showed a changed boot identity, active cryptsetup and mount units, the recovered LUKS mapping and XFS mount, and preserved marker data.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Direct before-and-after observations show RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 unchanged. The installed cryptsetup 2.0.3 package matches the existing 2.0.3 libraries, successfully operated LUKS1 through the legacy dm-crypt stack, and continued working after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The encrypted XFS volume was directly observed at /srv/secure, automatic recovery was proven through an actual node reboot with preserved data, and the RHEL release and kernel remained unchanged. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and agrees with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations. Only minor retained installation and diagnostic artifacts reduce operational hygiene.
limitations: Package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so overall RPM database health was not independently established.

Lifecycle snapshots inventory /tmp but not /var/tmp or the user's home directory; retention of the listed temporary artifacts is inferred from their creation and the absence of cleanup in the complete command timeline rather than from a final filesystem inventory.

operational_hygiene.summary: Core system mutations—installing cryptsetup, creating and configuring the encrypted volume, testing declarative activation, and rebooting—were causally connected to the task. No failed services or new listening endpoints were observed afterward. Minor hygiene defects remain: the complete timeline shows no cleanup of /var/tmp/secure-yum.log and secure-yum.pid created during repository discovery (cmd-40da2eb02df749a5), the downloaded RPM (cmd-419fc1fb674b4fc3), the downloaded signing key (cmd-2b7cbb880fba4173), the reboot log (cmd-2bcbf86dddb445f2), or the antrieb user's newly initialized ~/.gnupg files (cmd-a19152c47d3a40af). These were bounded, low-risk artifacts supporting necessary installation or verification work, but appear retained rather than restored or removed. No unrelated or security-weakening mutation was demonstrated.
